itineraries.title: Raleigh First Friday — Air Conditioning Until Sundown
itineraries.theme: A 100°F Friday spent indoors on purpose, then Moore Square once the sun is off the lawn
itineraries.drive_time: Downtown Raleigh, park once. Marbles, the Natural Sciences museum and Moore Square are within four blocks of each other; Raleigh Little Theatre is a 7-minute drive out to Pogue Street.
itineraries.cost_range: $25–$70 per person. Both museums' daily programs are free; Marbles IMAX and Hairspray are the paid legs.
itineraries.overview: The forecast high is 100°F — the hottest day of the window — so this route treats shade as the itinerary and not a detail. Free live-science programming at the Natural Sciences museum fills the middle of the day, IMAX handles the worst of the afternoon, and First Friday's market and movie at Moore Square only starts once the sun is low. If you want a full theatre night instead, Hairspray at Raleigh Little Theatre is the swap.

morning.title: Twinkle, Twinkle, Little Star
morning.notes: Twenty-five minutes, built for under-fives, and over before the heat arrives. Skip this leg if you have no small children — start at the museum instead.

morning.title: Live Animal Feeding — Ocean Habitat
morning.notes: Fifteen minutes, free, and the museum around it is free all day. This is the cheapest air conditioning downtown.

afternoon.title: The Blue Angels 3D
afternoon.notes: Marbles IMAX is a five-storey screen and a very cold room. Buy the IMAX ticket separately from museum admission if you only want the film.

afternoon.title: Incredible Science
afternoon.notes: A thirty-minute live demo in the Daily Planet theater. Free, and the walk back from Marbles is four shaded blocks on Hargett.

evening.title: First Friday Market and Movie: Remember the Titans
evening.notes: Vendors and food trucks from 5, live music at 5:30, film at 7:15. Bring a blanket; Moore Square's lawn holds heat well into the evening at 100°F, so the shaded north edge under the oaks is the better spot.

evening.title: Hairspray (alternative to the movie)
evening.notes: Two and a half hours with an intermission, fully indoors. Take this instead of Moore Square if the heat wins.

food.vegan_dish: The vegan 'pulled pork' BBQ plate — jackfruit, slaw, hush puppies
food.notes: Entirely vegetarian with most of the menu vegan or veganizable. Six blocks from Marbles on Dawson; reservations help on a Friday.

food.vegan_dish: Varies by truck — the First Friday lineup usually includes at least one all-vegan truck
food.notes: Eat on site so you keep your spot on the lawn. If the trucks look thin, Garland on Martin Street is a five-minute walk and its vegetable thali is fully vegan.

alternatives.leg: First Friday Market and Movie at Moore Square
alternatives.good_weather: Stay for the 7:15 PM film — by then the square is in full shade and the temperature drops fast.
alternatives.rain: Friday night carries a slight chance of showers and thunderstorms. If it breaks, Hairspray at Raleigh Little Theatre (7:30 PM, $30-$36) is the indoor swap, or the 8:00 PM Mostley Crue tribute at Lincoln Theatre two blocks from the square.

practical_notes: 100°F is a real hazard, not a talking point. Carry water, and plan the 12–4 block indoors as written.
Park once in the Wilmington Street deck (free on weekends until 5 PM, paid Friday) and walk everything downtown.
The Natural Sciences museum and Marbles both close at 5 PM; the museum's free programs are the anchor, not the IMAX.
Moore Square has no reserved seating. Arriving at 6:30 PM is enough for the 7:15 film.

itineraries.title: Durham Saturday — Market, Walking Tour, Melissa Etheridge
itineraries.theme: One walkable downtown from an 8 AM market to an 8 PM theatre, with storms in the second half

weather.summary: Sunny then Chance Showers And Thunderstorms

itineraries.drive_time: Park once near Foster Street. The market, the gallery, both tour meeting points and the Carolina Theatre are all inside a ten-minute walk.
itineraries.cost_range: $30–$85 per person. The market and the gallery are free; the walking tours are $15 each and Etheridge tickets are the big line item.
itineraries.overview: 98°F and sunny early, with a real chance of afternoon thunderstorms — the exact shape of day that rewards starting at eight. The Durham Farmers' Market opens then and thins by ten. The middle of the day is indoors at 5 Points Gallery and Outer Loop Arts, and the historian-guided tour at 2 PM is the one leg genuinely exposed to weather. Melissa Etheridge closes it in Fletcher Hall.

morning.title: Durham Farmers' Market
morning.notes: Go at eight, not ten. The DCP Pavilion is covered, which matters more for sun today than for rain.

morning.title: Field & Factory: A Look at Tobacco's Laborers
morning.notes: Free, at Duke Homestead, eight minutes north by car. Skip it if you would rather stay on foot downtown — the 1 PM gallery leg works as a straight substitute.

afternoon.title: THE LONG EXHALE | A GROUP EXHIBITION
afternoon.notes: Free, air-conditioned, and about half an hour unless you linger. 5 Points Gallery is a two-minute walk from the Lucky Strike Tower tour start.

afternoon.title: Downtown Durham Historian-Guided Tour
afternoon.notes: Ninety minutes on foot with very little shade at 98°F. Bring water. This is the leg to drop if the storms arrive early — the 4 PM African American history tour is the same price and the same length.

evening.title: Melissa Etheridge: RISE
evening.notes: Fletcher Hall at the Carolina Theatre, indoors and a five-minute walk from dinner on Parrish Street.

evening.title: BLAT / Homeostasis / The Band "&" (alternative)
evening.notes: Latin post-punk and darkwave at The Pinhook, 18+. The cheaper, louder version of the same night.

food.vegan_dish: Vegan glazed donut
food.notes: Eat before the market or graze the market's own pastry stalls, which are gone by nine.

food.vegan_dish: Vegan bibimbap with tofu, no egg
food.notes: On Parrish Street, indoors, and quick enough to make the 2 PM tour start.

food.vegan_dish: Vegan shoyu ramen — kombu-shiitake broth, no chashu, no egg
food.vegetarian_dish: Miso ramen with corn and butter
food.notes: Ask for the vegan broth specifically; the default shoyu is pork-based. Two blocks from the Carolina Theatre.

alternatives.leg: Downtown Durham Historian-Guided Tour (2 PM, outdoors)
alternatives.good_weather: Take the 2 PM tour as written and follow it with the 4 PM African American history tour from CCB Plaza if you still have legs.
alternatives.rain: Saturday afternoon carries a chance of showers and thunderstorms. Swap to Encaustic Painting at Outer Loop Arts (1 PM, $25) or Paint Pouring (3 PM, $25) — both indoors, both two hours.

alternatives.good_weather: Walk. Everything but Duke Homestead is inside ten minutes on foot.
alternatives.rain: The American Tobacco tunnel and the Chapel Hill Street awnings keep you dry between the gallery and the theatre.

practical_notes: 98°F with storms building: the market at 8 AM and the theatre at 8 PM are the fixed points, and the middle is negotiable.
Both walking tours are $15 and start from the Lucky Strike Tower or CCB Plaza — confirm the meeting point when you book.
Durham Central Park's Movies in the Park (7:30 PM, free) is the free alternative to Etheridge if the sky clears.
Street parking downtown is free on Saturdays.

itineraries.title: Chapel Hill & Carrboro — Cookout Market to Giant Puppets
itineraries.theme: Labor Day weekend on the west side: a meat-forward market, a planetarium dome, and Paperhand under the trees

weather.summary: Sunny then Chance Showers And Thunderstorms

itineraries.drive_time: About 30 minutes from Raleigh. Carrboro to Franklin Street is 5 minutes; Forest Theatre is a 10-minute drive or a long walk from downtown Chapel Hill.
itineraries.cost_range: $20–$55 per person. The market and the nature walk are free; the planetarium and Paperhand are the paid legs.
itineraries.overview: The Carrboro Farmers Market runs its Labor Day weekend Cookout on Saturday, putting local chicken, duck, pork, beef, lamb and bison farmers front and centre — worth the drive on its own. The 98°F afternoon goes into Morehead's planetarium dome, and the day ends at Forest Theatre, where Paperhand Puppet Intervention's giant-puppet show plays outdoors with a 6:20 PM opener.

morning.title: Carrboro Farmers Market: Carrboro Cookout
morning.notes: The Cookout is the market's meat showcase — six species, all local. Vegetarians are still well served by the produce and prepared-food stalls, which are the majority of the market.

morning.title: Family Nature Walks
morning.notes: Free, ninety minutes, run by Chapel Hill Public Library. Outdoors — go at ten or not at all today.

afternoon.title: We Are Stars
afternoon.location: 250 E Franklin St, Chapel Hill, NC 27599
afternoon.notes: Morehead's fulldome show, about 25 minutes, and the coldest dark room in Chapel Hill.

afternoon.title: From Earth to the Universe
afternoon.location: 250 E Franklin St, Chapel Hill, NC 27599
afternoon.notes: A second dome show if you are waiting out the worst of the heat. Carolina Skies at 4:30 PM is the live-narrated option.

evening.title: Paperhand Puppet Intervention: Wild Wisdom
evening.notes: Forest Theatre is an outdoor stone amphitheatre. Opener at 6:20, show at 7. Bring a cushion — the seats are stone — and bug spray.

food.vegan_dish: Not the place for it — go to Weaver Street Market's hot bar next door instead
food.notes: A hundred metres from the market. Weaver Street Market, in the same block, has a fully vegan section on its hot bar and outdoor lawn seating.

food.vegan_dish: Chana masala with coconut rice, no ghee — ask and they will make it vegan
food.notes: In Courtyard off Franklin Street, five minutes from Morehead. They label vegan dishes on the menu.

food.vegan_dish: Black bean burger, no cheese, on a vegan bun
food.vegetarian_dish: Black bean burger with pimento cheese
food.notes: Fast enough to eat before the 6:20 PM opener at Forest Theatre, which is a seven-minute drive away.

alternatives.leg: Paperhand Puppet Intervention at Forest Theatre (outdoors)
alternatives.good_weather: Arrive by 6:15 for the opener and a decent seat — the stone amphitheatre fills up.
alternatives.rain: Saturday evening turns to showers and thunderstorms likely. Paperhand cancels for weather rather than moving indoors, so check their site the afternoon of. The indoor swap is Schur with Fai Laci at Cat's Cradle Back Room (8 PM) — six minutes from Carrboro.

alternatives.good_weather: Fine at ten; it will already be in the high 80s.
alternatives.rain: Move it indoors to Morehead early — the 10:30 AM Magic Tree House Space Mission is aimed at the same age group.

practical_notes: The Carrboro market is cash-and-card, but several farmers are cash-preferred — bring some.
Forest Theatre has no parking lot of its own; use the Country Club Road spaces and walk in.
98°F with evening storms: the outdoor legs are bookends, and the middle of the day is deliberately in a dome.
Morehead sells dome shows individually; you do not need the exhibit ticket.

itineraries.title: Labor Day in Durham — Playground Pints and a 5:05 First Pitch
itineraries.theme: The one genuinely comfortable day of the week, spent mostly outside
itineraries.drive_time: Everything is downtown Durham. The Glass Jug to the ballpark is a 12-minute walk; park once at American Tobacco.
itineraries.cost_range: $20–$50 per person. The playground afternoon is free; Bulls tickets start low and the Pinhook show is the optional add-on.
itineraries.overview: 85°F and mostly sunny — after three days at 98–100°F this is the day to be outdoors, and the schedule leans into it. Pints at the Playground runs free all afternoon at the Glass Jug downtown, the Bulls play Nashville at 5:05 in the last home stand of the season, and if you still have a night in you, The Pinhook has an all-ages electronic bill at 7:30.

morning.title: Live Animal Feeding — Ocean Habitat
morning.notes: Only if you are starting from Raleigh — it is a 30-minute drive to Durham afterwards. Otherwise sleep in; the day does not really begin until two.

afternoon.title: Pints at the Playground
afternoon.notes: Free, outdoors, four hours, and explicitly built for adults with small children. The Glass Jug downtown is a 12-minute walk from the ballpark, so you can leave straight for first pitch.

evening.title: Durham Bulls vs. Nashville Sounds
evening.notes: A Labor Day afternoon start. At 85°F the third-base concourse holds the shade; the Blue Monster side bakes until about seven.

evening.title: Spike Hellis / NUXX / Corpse Dust
evening.notes: All ages, at The Pinhook, four blocks from the ballpark. Only worth it if you leave the game around the seventh.

food.vegan_dish: Jamaican jerk jackfruit bowl from the Caribbean stall
food.vegetarian_dish: Margherita from the wood-fired pizza counter
food.notes: Several counters under one roof, so a mixed group can sort itself out. Air-conditioned, and eight minutes from the Glass Jug.

food.vegan_dish: The ballpark's veggie dog, ordered plain
food.notes: Thin pickings for vegans. If that matters, eat at the food hall first and treat the game as dessert.

alternatives.leg: Durham Bulls vs. Nashville Sounds (outdoors, 5:05 PM)
alternatives.good_weather: Mostly sunny at 85°F — the best baseball weather of the week. Sit on the third-base side.
alternatives.rain: No rain in the Labor Day forecast, but if a cell moves through, Line Dancing at Motorco (7 PM, free) and Trivia Night Mondays at Ponysaurus (6:30 PM) are both indoors and both within a mile.

alternatives.good_weather: Four hours in the open. Sunscreen; there is limited shade.
alternatives.rain: Move it to Outer Loop Arts — Paint Pouring or the Printmaking Workshop, both 6 PM and $25.

practical_notes: This is the last Bulls home stand of the season — Nashville is in town Monday, Wednesday and Thursday.
85°F and mostly sunny is the mildest day in the window; the two days either side are near 90°F and the three before it are near 100°F.
American Tobacco parking decks are the easy option and put you between the Glass Jug, the ballpark and dinner.
Marbles Kids Museum is closed Monday through Friday this week; do not plan a Durham-plus-Marbles day.

itineraries.title: Hopscotch Opening Night — Free Day Parties, Then the Real Thing
itineraries.theme: Downtown Raleigh on the first day of Hopscotch, starting with the shows that cost nothing
itineraries.drive_time: All downtown Raleigh and all walkable. Slim's, Kings, the Pour House, Lincoln Theatre and City Plaza sit within three blocks of each other.
itineraries.cost_range: $0–$180 per person. The day parties are free; a 3-day GA pass is $179 and VIP is $399.
itineraries.overview: Hopscotch runs September 10–12 across City Plaza, Moore Square and a ring of downtown clubs. Thursday is opening day, and it starts with free, unbadged day parties: the Wake Forest Listening Room takes Slim's from noon, and Hopscotch Goes Hardcore runs free at the Pour House from 12:30. Dexter and The Moonrocks close the City Plaza stage that night. You can do the whole afternoon for nothing and decide about a pass afterwards.

morning.title: Public Library Pop-Up
morning.notes: Free, two hours, at Gipson Play Plaza in Dix Park. A quiet start before downtown fills up — and a ten-minute drive from the day parties.

afternoon.title: The Wake Forest Listening Room Presents
afternoon.notes: Free show, doors at noon, five hours of it at Slim's. No festival pass needed.

afternoon.title: (DAY) Hopscotch Goes Hardcore
afternoon.notes: Commitment, Muscle, Mean Habit and more, free at the Pour House. Doors noon. Two blocks from Slim's, so you can move between them.

evening.title: Hopscotch Music Festival 2026
evening.notes: City Plaza is the outdoor main stage. Dexter and The Moonrocks close Thursday, with Momma and Liz Cooper also on the day's bill.

evening.title: Hopscotch Music Festival — Night 1 (Lincoln Theatre)
evening.notes: Club shows run in parallel with the plaza — Lincoln Theatre and Kings (from 9 PM) are both official venues, and a GA pass covers them.

food.vegan_dish: Vegan pho with tofu and mushroom broth
food.notes: Laotian, on Blount Street between Slim's and the Pour House. Ask for the vegetarian broth — the default is bone-based.

food.vegan_dish: The vegetable thali, ordered vegan — most of the components already are
food.notes: Same block as Bida Manda, and it stays open late enough to eat between the plaza and the club shows.

alternatives.good_weather: September 10 is at the edge of the National Weather Service forecast horizon, so there is no verified forecast for it yet — check before you go.
alternatives.rain: The club shows are the built-in rain plan: Lincoln Theatre, Kings, Nash Hall, Neptunes, Slim's and the Pour House are all indoors and all covered by the same pass.

alternatives.good_weather: The free day parties make this work with no pass at all.
alternatives.rain: Both day parties are indoors already.

practical_notes: The noon and 12:30 day parties are free and do not require a festival pass — that is the cheap way into opening day.
A 3-day GA pass is $179 and VIP is $399; single-day passes exist but were not priced on the passes page.
Official venues this year: City Plaza, Moore Square, King's, Lincoln Theatre, Nash Hall, Neptunes, Slims and The Pour House.
Downtown parking decks fill early on a festival Thursday — the Wilmington Street deck is the closest to the cluster.

itineraries.title: Pittsboro & Chatham County — Markets, Tigers, Sculpture
itineraries.theme: The slow-lane version of Saturday, 45 minutes west of Raleigh

weather.summary: Sunny then Chance Showers And Thunderstorms

itineraries.drive_time: About 45 minutes from Raleigh to Pittsboro. Chatham Mills to Fearrington is 8 minutes; Carolina Tiger Rescue is 15 minutes south.
itineraries.cost_range: $15–$50 per person. The market and the wine tasting are free; the tiger tour is the paid centrepiece.
itineraries.overview: Chatham County runs on a different clock, which suits a 98°F Saturday. The Chatham Mills market opens at eight, the Belted Goat pours free wine at one, and the day builds to Twilight Tours at Carolina Tiger Rescue at five — deliberately timed for when the big cats actually move. Old-Fashioned Farmers' Days at Silk Hope is the bigger-festival alternative if you want a full day outdoors.

morning.title: Chatham Mills Farmers Market
morning.notes: Eight to noon, and worth being early for at 98°F. The mill building behind it has shade and a coffee counter.

morning.title: Old-Fashioned Farmers' Days (alternative)
morning.notes: A two-day heritage festival at Silk Hope Farm Heritage Park — antique tractors, crafts, demonstrations. About 50 minutes from Raleigh and almost entirely outdoors, so it is the good-weather-only option today.

afternoon.title: Come Out and Play Sculpture Show
afternoon.notes: An outdoor sculpture show across a 17-acre homestead, open until eight. Walkable in an hour; there is tree cover across much of it.

afternoon.title: Free Wine Tastings at The Belted Goat
afternoon.notes: Free, indoors, two hours, in Fearrington Village. The right place to sit out the hottest part of the day.

evening.title: Twilight Tours at Carolina Tiger Rescue
evening.notes: Guided, outdoors, and timed for when tigers, lions and caracals get active. Book ahead — twilight tours sell out. Closed shoes required.

evening.title: Live Music at Galloway's
evening.notes: The alternative evening if you skip the tigers — two hours of live music back in Fearrington Village.

food.vegan_dish: Whatever the bakery stall has without butter — ask; several Chatham bakers do vegan runs
food.vegetarian_dish: Egg-and-cheese biscuit from the prepared-food vendors
food.notes: Eat at the market rather than hunting for a cafe — Pittsboro is small and Saturday mornings are busy.

food.vegan_dish: Hummus and roasted vegetable sandwich, no aioli
food.notes: On the Pittsboro circle, air-conditioned, and quick. Locally known as The MOD.

food.vegan_dish: Ask for the vegetable plate built vegan — the kitchen does it on request
food.notes: Back at Chatham Mills, so you end where you started. Live piano on Tuesdays and Thursdays, not Saturdays.

alternatives.leg: Twilight Tours at Carolina Tiger Rescue (outdoors, 5 PM)
alternatives.good_weather: Go as written — five to eight is exactly when the cats are worth watching.
alternatives.rain: Saturday evening turns to thunderstorms likely. The rescue cancels tours in lightning, so call ahead. The indoor swap is Live Music at Galloway's in Fearrington (5 PM) or a drive back to Cat's Cradle in Carrboro (8 PM).

alternatives.leg: Come Out and Play Sculpture Show (outdoors, midday)
alternatives.good_weather: Fine, but go for the tree-covered sections at 98°F.
alternatives.rain: Swap to the free Belted Goat tasting earlier and stay indoors in Fearrington.

practical_notes: Carolina Tiger Rescue requires closed-toe shoes and advance booking; it is a sanctuary, not a zoo, and tours run rain-or-shine except in lightning.
Chatham County is 40-50 minutes from Raleigh — comfortably a same-day trip, but do not plan to bounce back and forth.
98°F with evening storms: the free indoor tasting at 1 PM is the deliberate heat break.
Several Chatham market vendors are cash-preferred.

itineraries.title: A Free Raleigh Thursday — Museums, Trivia, Zero Cover
itineraries.theme: How far a Thursday goes on nothing but free admission
itineraries.drive_time: Downtown Raleigh, walkable end to end. The Gregg Museum is a 10-minute drive out to Hillsborough Street.
itineraries.cost_range: $0–$25 per person. Every scheduled leg here is free; you only pay for food and drinks.
itineraries.overview: 98°F and sunny, and this route never charges admission. The Gregg Museum's Black heritage exhibition and the Natural Sciences museum are both free and both cold, Science Trivia at seven is free, and Compass Rose runs free trivia the same night if you would rather have a beer in your hand. It is the cheapest good day in the window.

morning.title: Community Stories: Sustaining North Carolina's Black Heritage
morning.notes: At the Gregg Museum of Art & Design on the NC State campus. Free, indoors, and rarely crowded on a weekday morning.

afternoon.title: Public Tour
afternoon.notes: The NCMA's free daily tour of the West Building. The museum's collection galleries are free every day; only special exhibitions charge.

afternoon.title: Adaptive Tai Chi in the Park
afternoon.notes: In the NCMA Museum Park at the Welcome Center. Outdoors at 98°F, so this is the leg to skip if the heat has already won.

evening.title: Science Trivia
evening.notes: Free, an hour, at the Natural Sciences museum. Teams form on the night; you do not need to bring one.

evening.title: Trivia Night at Compass Rose (alternative)
evening.notes: No entry fee, and there is beer. The version of the same evening for people who do not want to do trivia sober.

food.vegan_dish: Collards cooked without meat plus black-eyed peas and rice — ask, they do it
food.vegetarian_dish: Mac and cheese with two vegetable sides
food.notes: Meat-and-three format, so the vegetable plate is a genuine meal rather than a consolation.

food.vegan_dish: Seasonal vegetable plate, built vegan on request
food.notes: In the museum itself, so it slots between the tour and tai chi without moving the car.

alternatives.leg: Adaptive Tai Chi in the Park (outdoors, 5 PM)
alternatives.good_weather: Sunny at 98°F — go only if you tolerate heat well, and hydrate first.
alternatives.rain: Thursday is clear, so heat rather than rain is the risk. The indoor swap is staying in the NCMA galleries until the museum closes.

practical_notes: The NCMA collection galleries, the Natural Sciences museum and the Gregg Museum are all free every day — this itinerary costs nothing but food.
98°F: the outdoor tai chi leg is genuinely optional, and the rest of the day is air-conditioned.
NCMA parking is free. Downtown at the Natural Sciences museum, the Wilmington Street deck is the closest.
Science Trivia fills up; get there by 6:45.

itineraries.title: Cary & Apex — Market, Film Screen, Free Outdoor Movie
itineraries.theme: A western-Wake family Saturday that ends on a lawn

weather.summary: Sunny then Chance Showers And Thunderstorms

itineraries.drive_time: 20 minutes from Raleigh to Cary. Downtown Cary Park to the Cary Theater is a two-minute walk; Apex is 12 minutes further southwest.
itineraries.cost_range: $15–$45 per person. The market and Friday's movie are free; the Cary Theater screenings and the Halle programme are the paid legs.
itineraries.overview: Downtown Cary has quietly become the easiest family Saturday in the Triangle: the farmers market runs 8 to noon in the park, the Cary Theater screens all afternoon two minutes away, and Apex's Halle Cultural Arts Center adds a kids' morning. At 98°F the theatre is the point — it is the only cold room in downtown Cary that holds a crowd.

morning.title: Cary Farmers Market
morning.notes: Eight to noon at Downtown Cary Park. The park's splash area is the reason to bring children early on a 98°F day.

morning.title: SuperFun Saturday
morning.notes: Two hours of activities at the Halle Cultural Arts Center in downtown Apex, 12 minutes from Cary. Indoors.

afternoon.title: Cookie Queens
afternoon.notes: At the Cary Theater, a restored single-screen on Chatham Street. Cold, dark, and two minutes from the park.

afternoon.title: The Sun Never Sets
afternoon.notes: The second screening if you are waiting out the heat — or skip it and head to Durham for Movies in the Park.

evening.title: Movies in the Park: DPR's Fall Film Series
evening.notes: Free and outdoors in Durham Central Park, 25 minutes away. The Cary equivalent, Movie Night: Hamilton, ran the night before on Friday.

food.vegan_dish: Ask the bakery vendors — several bring vegan pastries
food.notes: Eat in the park before it gets hot; there is shade on the eastern edge.

food.vegan_dish: Falafel plate with hummus, tabbouleh and no yoghurt sauce
food.notes: On Chatham Street, a block from the theatre, and reliably quick before a 2 PM screening.

food.vegan_dish: Marinara pie, no cheese — the crust and sauce are both vegan
food.notes: Neapolitan, small room, worth booking. Eat here and skip the drive to Durham if the evening film is not worth 25 minutes each way.

alternatives.leg: Movies in the Park in Durham (outdoors, 7:30 PM)
alternatives.good_weather: Free and on the grass — bring a blanket and get there by seven.
alternatives.rain: Showers and thunderstorms are likely Saturday evening. The indoor swap is a third Cary Theater screening, or Trivia Night at Downtown Cary Park the following Thursday if you would rather stay local.

alternatives.good_weather: Sunny and already warm by nine — go at eight.
alternatives.rain: The market runs rain or shine; the park's covered structures handle a passing shower.

practical_notes: Downtown Cary Park has free parking decks on Academy Street and a splash pad that matters at 98°F.
The Cary Theater sells tickets through Etix; prices are not shown on the listing page.
BEYOND: The Cary Film Festival opens at the same theatre on September 10 — worth knowing if this Saturday works out.
Apex's Halle Cultural Arts Center is on Salem Street with street parking around the block.
